subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-09-09 - Rubenstein redeems the Kennedy Center's orphaned sculpture
html:
Nariway Signals
Tuesday, September 9, 2026
Lead
David Rubenstein bought the Kennedy Center sculpture Trump had dismantled — and is giving it to the National Gallery of Art
Joel Shapiro's 24-foot "Blue" — installed in 2019, torn down without notice last week on orders described as wanting "all new art for the reopening" — passed first to the artist's own foundation, as this brief noted Sept 3, and now to Rubenstein, the Kennedy Center's own former chairman, ousted from its board by Trump in 2025. He paid roughly $2M and will install it in the National Gallery's sculpture garden.
It closes the loop this brief has tracked all month on what happens when a government acts as a founder whose donor intent nobody can enforce: here, a private collector — the same one Trump pushed out — simply buys the orphaned gift back and re-homes it in the one federal collection built to outlast any single administration.
ARTnews  ·  Hyperallergic  ·  The Hill
What's happening
A Spanish bank just opened a €40M museum for a 1,000-work art collection five centuries deep
Faro Santander opened Sept 8 inside the bank's own 1795 former headquarters on the Bay of Santander, redesigned by David Chipperfield and financed by the Santander Foundation — Titian, Velázquez, Rubens, Goya, El Greco, Zurbarán, van Dyck, Sorolla, Miró and Picasso, plus a coin collection spanning the 2nd century BCE. A clean, current instance of the corporate-collection-to-public-museum pathway — except here the museum's building is the bank's own former home.
The Art Newspaper
Hungary's new government has formally killed a €250M national gallery seven years after it stalled
A June decree ends all construction on Budapest's SANAA-designed New National Gallery, halted since 2019 by the city's green mayor over environmental objections. The most decisive "abandoned museum plan" this brief has logged — not paused or defunded, but legally terminated — leaving Hungary's national collection with no confirmed future home.
The Art Newspaper
The Smithsonian's Lonnie Bunch is retiring, right as the White House fights to reshape the institution
Bunch, 73 — the Smithsonian's first Black and first historian Secretary — says pressure from the Trump administration over how the institution portrays American history played no role in his decision, and will stay three to four months to ease a transition. Another entry in the museum-leadership churn this brief has tracked for five straight weeks, landing this time at the institution most directly in the government's sights.
The Art Newspaper  ·  CNN
A Bangkok museum built to honor a collector's late father just landed its first luxury-brand partnership
Dib Bangkok — opened December 2025 by Purat "Chang" Osathanugrah, who took up the mantle of his father Petch's private, 1,000-plus-work collection and made it public across 11 halls — is now Chanel Culture Fund's first Southeast Asian partner. A second-generation legacy museum barely nine months old, already drawing the kind of institutional partnership older founder-museums spend years courting.
ARTnews
Berlin Art Week opened today with private collectors' own homes on public view for the first time
The festival's 15th edition (Sept 9–13) includes "Discovering Collections," guided tours through Berlin private collectors' houses that have never before opened to visitors — a rare, deliberately temporary reversal of the usual direction this brief tracks, where a private collection becomes a permanent public space rather than a five-day peek behind a door that closes again.
Berlin Art Week
Worth reading
Grossman LLP on a second win shielding art authenticators from a disgruntled dealer's lawsuit
A New York court has now twice dismissed London dealer James Mayor's decade-old suit against the Agnes Martin catalogue raisonné committee over 13 works it declined to authenticate — a precedent directly relevant to any collection whose value depends on a committee's say, and to the appraisal-and-authentication risk sitting inside the art-lending market this brief tracks.
Grossman LLP
Marion Maneker on Leon Black's buy-low-sell-high approach to collecting
"Wall Power" (Puck) takes a close read of one of the art world's most consequential financier-collectors' actual trading discipline — treating masterpieces as a portfolio to be managed, not just accumulated — a useful counterpoint to every legacy-and-permanence story this brief otherwise tracks.
Puck
For the record
Thieves stole two Renoirs worth roughly €9M from the artist's own house-museum in a three-minute raid
A pair sliced through a fence and a window at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer before dawn Sept 8, dropping two of four paintings in the garden as they fled; two works remain missing, and France's cultural-goods trafficking office has joined the investigation. A second museum-theft data point in as many weeks for anyone advising on collection security.
Euronews  ·  CBC
Collector Libbie Mugrabi lost her Hamptons house to sidewalk foreclosure the same day she sued her art lenders
Mugrabi filed suit against Art Capital Group's principals roughly 90 minutes after her mortgage lender filed foreclosure on the Sag Harbor estate she'd stopped paying since April 2023; her suit accuses the pair of interfering with a planned sale of her $30M Basquiat and a $1.5M Warhol pledged as loan collateral. A vivid, personal-scale illustration of exactly the appraisal-and-liquidity risk sitting inside the growing art-secured lending market.
Artnet
Clive Davis's estate is sending eight paintings worth $35M+ to Christie's November New York sales
The Warhol/Hockney/Mitchell/Stella/Condo/Motherwell group includes a Warhol portrait of Aretha Franklin (Davis discovered and championed her), starting bidding at $2M — a fresh entry in the November marquee-week single-owner pipeline this brief is tracking alongside the $450M Blaquier collection.
ARTnews
To see (escalating)
Christie's Alan Medaugh Hiroshige preview is now 2 days out
Public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 20 Rockefeller Plaza; already on Alina's calendar for the Sept 12 preview. ARTnews
The Bartos Mondrian's Paris leg opens today; the free New York leg is 8 days out
Public-view legs: Paris Sept 9–12, New York Sept 17–20, Hong Kong Sept 25–29, London from Oct 8, sale Oct 14 (£20–30M / $27–41M estimate). ARTnews
The Rothschild collection preview at Artcurial is now 8 days out
"Le goût Rothschild en héritage" — public preview Sept 17–22, sale Sept 22, Paris. Artcurial
Sotheby's Open House (Sept 20–21, NYC) is now 11 days out
Its confirmed program includes a session on legal considerations across an art collection's lifecycle, staged by the house's own trusts-and-estates practice. Sotheby's
Rooms to be in
Next up: EPC of Westchester County's Fall Networking Event — 14 days out
Sept 23, Freebird Kitchen & Bar, 5pm. Non-members explicitly welcome (~$85), the lowest-pressure first visit to any of the four target councils.
Forward pipeline:
  • Sept 17 — Matrons Mixer (Hall Rockefeller/Less Than Half), New York — registered, now 8 days out
  • Sept 17–22 — Rothschild preview at Artcurial, Paris (see To see, fly-and-stay)
  • Sept 20–21 — Sotheby's Open House, NYC (see To see)
  • Sept 23 — two CE webinars registered, plus the Westchester event above the same evening — worth stacking
  • Oct 5 — EPC of New York City's "Making Sense of AI" evening (confirm venue/fee)
  • Oct 21 — EPC of Westchester's dinner meeting, White Plains
  • Nov 12 — EPC of Bergen County breakfast, Wyckoff, NJ
  • Nov 17 — EPC of NYC's "Art Financing as an Important Tool for Wealth & Estate Planning" — already registered, Alina's first confirmed room
